objective_constant: Design a rigorous empirical study to determine whether the same large-language-model question can produce meaningfully different responses, why such changes occur, and how to distinguish true response instability from ordinary wording variation. Produce a research plan only. Do not run experiments and do not use external tools.

conditions.label: No additional methodological frame
conditions.instruction: Use your best methodological judgment. Do not assume any specific named framework.

conditions.label: Local perturbation / finite-difference
conditions.instruction: Use a local perturbation perspective. Identify state variables, hold relevant factors fixed, vary one input factor at a time, and measure which output components change relative to a baseline noise floor.

conditions.label: Bayesian
conditions.instruction: Use a Bayesian research perspective. State competing hypotheses, prior uncertainty, what observations would update those beliefs, and how posterior uncertainty would affect conclusions and stopping decisions.

conditions.label: Falsificationist
conditions.instruction: Use a falsification-first research perspective. Define claims so they can fail, prioritize severe tests and counterexamples, and specify in advance what observations would refute each central hypothesis.

conditions.label: Causal inference
conditions.instruction: Use a causal-inference perspective. Define treatments, outcomes, confounders, controls and counterfactual comparisons, and separate causal effects of prompt changes from stochastic variation and measurement error.

conditions.label: State-space / dynamical systems
conditions.instruction: Use a state-space perspective. Define an observable state vector, distinguish independent variability from sequential transitions, and specify transition, stability, path-dependence, and perturbation measurements without claiming unobserved internal states.

conditions.label: Software / metamorphic testing
conditions.instruction: Use a software-testing perspective. Define invariants, metamorphic relations, test oracles, boundary cases, regression tests, failure classes, and a reproducible test harness for the research question.
